messages:
Claire (PM): Heads-up — BigCorp asked for a strict pin + 12mo stability SLA for their model fleet. They want bench parity with current v1 on throughput and <50ms p50. Need a decision on scope: do we accept a hard pin (no auto-migration) or offer a 'soft pin' with guaranteed fallback?
Raj (Eng): Do we have perf data on the v1 -> v2 delta for their typical sequence lengths? quick guess: v2 is 10-15% faster on long seqs but has higher cold-start variance.
Eli (SRE): Cold-start variance is the real issue for the p50 target. If we promise <50ms p50 we need either prewarmed dedicated slots or a higher-tail mitigation (prefix cache priming).
Jose (AE): From the account: they will pay for reserved capacity if we can formalize it. They've been explicit that migrations must not degrade customer UX.
Marta (Customer): Confirming — we need zero surprise rollouts. We can sign reserved capacity + a 90-day notice before any migration.
Claire (PM): Options we discussed: (A) Hard pin: customer picks exact model hash and we freeze auto-updates; requires explicit manual rollover and increases support load. (B) Soft pin: we keep them on an older variant but offer a compatibility shim + optional canary on demand. (C) Hybrid: initial hard pin for 6 months, then transition to soft pin with opt-in rollouts. Thoughts?
Raj (Eng): Hybrid seems pragmatic. Implementation-wise a hard pin means excluding them from the routing policy that auto-rolls to v2. That's trivial. The complexity is ensuring we still push security/patch fixes to pinned variants — do we allow patchbackport?
Eli (SRE): We should require patchbackports for critical CVEs and infra fixes. Also need an operational runbook: if pinned fleet falls behind perf targets, ops should have an automated alert and an emergency canary path to a fallback model.
Claire (PM): Acceptance criteria I'm proposing for the pinned SLA: 1) p50 <50ms for their top-3 endpoints, measured over a 30d rolling window; 2) 99.9% availability; 3) 12mo pin with 90-day notice for migrations; 4) reserved capacity contract signed. If any of 1-2 break, we trigger remediation.
Jose (AE): Sales will need a simple one-pager for legal: pin length, rollback policy, performance SLOs, and breach remedies. I can draft.
Raj (Eng): Bench plan: we run their synthetic prompt set against pinned variant on dedicated hosts (match customer's region + instance type). I'll own the bench run. Need the prompt set + typical concurrency numbers.
Marta (Customer): Shared prompt set uploaded to our S3 link earlier — can you confirm you have access? concurrency ~ 50 qps for the primary flow, spiky bursts to 200 qps.
Eli (SRE): For <50ms p50 at 50 qps we probably need a pool of warmed GPUs with continuous batching disabled for that lane. That increases cost substantially. Need finance sign-off.
Claire (PM): Tradeoff call: we can either reduce latency target to 60ms and avoid reserved prewarm costs, or accept the higher reserved cost for 50ms. Which direction?
Jose (AE): Customer is price-sensitive but prioritizes UX. They'll likely accept a price uplift if it's presented as a reserved-lane premium. I'll float both options.
Raj (Eng): Implementation checklist from eng side: - bench harness run (owner: Raj) - pin routing flag + exclusion from auto-roll (owner: Raj) - patchbackport policy documented (owner: Claire/Raj) - canary emergency path (owner: Eli)
Eli (SRE): Ops checklist: - alerting thresholds for p50 and availability - runbook for emergency failover - cost tracking per pin lane - dashboard tile in Console for their tenant
Claire (PM): Timeline proposal: Week 0: sign contract + get prompt set. Week 1: bench run and perf report. Week 2: implement routing pin + test canary. Week 3: soft launch into reserved lane. Does that feel reasonable?
Raj (Eng): Week 1 bench run might take 3-4 days; add another week for canary tests. So W0 sign -> W3 gate is tight but doable if we parallelize.
Marta (Customer): We can expedite contract review if you share the one-pager today.
Jose (AE): I'll share a draft by EOD. Claire, can you review before I send?
Claire (PM): Yes — I'll review. Action items: Jose draft legal one-pager; Raj schedule bench job and request S3 access; Eli draft ops runbook; Claire finalize acceptance criteria and pin policy doc.
deploy-bot: scheduled bench-job-1732111001 started by Raj
Raj (Eng): bench run kicked off, including latency histograms and token-level cost estimates. Will post results as soon as available.
Eli (SRE): Noted — I'm adding a temporary dashboard tile for the tenant while we validate metrics.
Claire (PM): Thanks everyone. If bench shows >50ms p50 at realistic concurrency we'll present the two options to the customer (latency vs cost uplift). Will post summary after bench completes.
Raj (Eng): preliminary numbers: p50 = 48ms at 50 qps, p95 = 110ms, cold-start p50 spikes to ~300ms for new autoscale events. Need runbook for cold starts.
Eli (SRE): That's consistent. Plan: reserved warm pool + automated prefix priming during low-traffic windows reduces cold-start p50 to ~60-80ms.
Marta (Customer): That tradeoff is acceptable if you commit to the warm pool approach and explicit weekly health reports.
Claire (PM): Accept. We'll add weekly health reports to the SOW. Closing loop — draft SOW will include: pin length, reserved-lane pricing, acceptance criteria, patch policy, weekly health reports, emergency canary path.
Jose (AE): Sending draft SOW now. Claire, Raj, Eli please review — try to turn around comments by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Claire (PM): Reviewing now. Thanks everyone!
